issues.description: Script uses GM_xmlhttpRequest to access SponsorBlock API and multiple Cobalt instances for video download. These are third-party servers and may receive YouTube video IDs and possibly other metadata.
issues.recommendation: Review privacy policy of SponsorBlock and Cobalt instances. Limit data sent to only necessary video IDs. Warn users about potential privacy implications.

issues.description: Script stores toggle settings and state using GM_setValue/GM_getValue. No evidence of sensitive data collection (cookies, form fields, clipboard, etc.), but persistent storage is used.
issues.recommendation: Ensure only non-sensitive preferences are stored. Do not store user credentials or personal information.

issues.description: No evidence of eval, new Function, setTimeout(string), setInterval(string), or dynamic script injection. No @require of remote JS libraries.
issues.recommendation: Continue to avoid remote code execution patterns.

issues.description: No evidence of code obfuscation, base64 decoding, unicode encoding, or minified single-line code.
No evidence of DOM XSS or injection. User input is not inserted into innerHTML/outerHTML, nor is document.write used.
issues.recommendation: Continue to sanitize any future user input before DOM insertion.

issues.description: Script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest, GM_setValue, GM_getValue, GM_addStyle. All are used in code. No evidence of unused high-privilege grants.
Script connects to multiple Cobalt instances for video download. These are not official YouTube APIs and may pose supply chain risks.
issues.recommendation: Warn users about potential supply chain risks. Prefer official or well-known APIs when possible.

details: Persistent storage of toggle settings (adEnabled, sbEnabled, qualityEnabled) via GM_setValue/GM_getValue

script_name: EasyTube V3 — Ad Skip, SponsorBlock & HD Download⬇️🚀
summary: The script transmits YouTube video IDs and possibly other metadata to third-party servers (SponsorBlock and multiple Cobalt instances) for ad skipping and video downloading. No evidence of sensitive privacy collection or code execution risks. Supply chain risk exists due to reliance on unofficial Cobalt APIs. Users should be aware of potential privacy implications and supply chain risks.
